thread:
mona: heads-up — since the deploy last night we started seeing intermittent DNS failures from edge-gpu nodes in apac. pods trying to reach internal service names sometimes get NXDOMAIN, sometimes time out. broken for both k8s svc names and our internal registry :confused:

mona: snippet from one node's resolv.conf:
```
# /etc/resolv.conf (container view)
nameserver 127.0.0.53
search svc.cluster.local cluster.local redwood.internal.company
options ndots:5 timeout:1
```

raj: is that systemd-resolved stub? 127.0.0.53 suggests so. are you seeing different behavior if you query the upstream directly?

mona: yes, systemd stub. dig @127.0.0.53 ml-models.svc.cluster.local +short sometimes returns nothing, but `dig @10.0.0.10 ml-models.svc.cluster.local` (kube-dns) returns pod IP. flipping between them. sometimes queries seem to get forwarded to 1.1.1.1 (weird)

carl: this smells like ndots+long search path combinatorics. with ndots:5 glibc will try absolute then append each search entry — that can blow up and trigger timeouts if the stub resolver gives up early. also systemd-resolved has a split-horizon mode that can prefer upstreams for some queries.

kevin: i pushed a temporary iptables NAT rule to force stub -> kube-dns on the node level, so containers bypass 127.0.0.53 for cluster.svc queries. quick snippet:
```bash
# redirect queries for cluster.local to kube-dns (10.0.0.10)
iptables -t nat -A OUTPUT -p udp --dport 53 -d 127.0.0.53 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.0.0.10
```

raj: nice. does that avoid the 8.8.8.8 excursions? we saw some nodes hitting Cloudflare/Google which caused split-horizon failures when internal names leaked.

kevin: yes, after the rule the node's queries are stable. but it's tactical — we shouldn't rely on iptables forever.

mona: hypothesis: after the recent calico/kube-proxy change we increased search path length (added redwood.internal.company) and systemd-resolved started trying upstreams earlier because of concurrent query limits. observed per-node resolv stats: total queries spikes and ~12% SERVFAILs during spikes.

carl: long-term options:
- reduce ndots to 2 in base image or kubelet resolvConf patch
- disable systemd stub on GPU nodes and write static resolv.conf to point at kube-dns
- add explicit dnsPolicy/ndots override on critical pods

raj: agree. also add a probe in node provisioning to validate resolv.conf+dig for cluster SRV records before marking ready.

sre-bot: @oncall ping — DNS degradation detected in apac-gpu-edge, affecting ~4% of nodes, automated mitigation applied.

mona: rolling a conservative fix now: kubelet patch to set ndots:2 on new pods + config rollout to remove redwood.internal.company from search on user-facing nodes. monitoring dashboard alert set for SERVFAIL rate.

kevin: created K8S-DEV ticket with iptables snippet and proposed kubelet change. i can add a one-line systemd drop-in to stop the stub on private nodes if we choose.

carl: please document the root cause once confirmed. create postmortem if recurrence >1hr or >5% impact. :+1:

mona: created INC-7891 and added notes + logs. will follow up in the morning with full timeline. thanks all for the quick triage. :sparkles:
